trials.label: revise
trials.detail: [fable/medium] Not done. The share handlers are written but never mounted: apps/api/internal/http/routes.go registers only the schedules routes, so both share endpoints are unreachable on the real API. The passing verify is empty evidence, because `make test` is `true` and the tests rely on helpers that do not exist in the repo. Beyond those two blockers, links are saved without an expiry, and the Create response does not match the ShareLink contract the web button consumes; the button itself is not wired to anything. | BLOCKS (blocker/high): share.Register is never called. The API's route table (http.Register) only calls schedules.Register, and nothing else in the repo references share.Register. Neither POST /schedules/:id/share nor GET /share/:token is reachable on the real server, so the first three acceptance criteria do not hold in the running app. | BLOCKS (blocker/high): `make test` is just `true`, so the verify output "ok" is no evidence. No Go or web test was executed. The Go tests use assertStatus, post, get, owner, stranger and tok, none of which are defined anywhere in the repo; the web test uses render, screen and click with no imports. As written they likely do not compile, so no acceptance criterion is shown by a test that ran. | BLOCKS (major/medium): Links().Save(tok, s.ID) stores no expiry, and its result is ignored, yet Get relies on l.Expired() and the contract's ShareLink has expiresAt. Depending on the zero value, links either never expire or are expired at once (which would make every GET 404). A failed save also still returns 201 with a token that does not work. | BLOCKS (major/medium): Create responds with only {"token"}, while the web ShareButton takes a ShareLink {token, scheduleId, expiresAt} from @app/contract. Nothing in the web app calls the POST or renders ShareButton, so the button is not wired to the API, and if it were, the label would read "valid until undefined".

trials.label: revise
trials.detail: [fable/medium] The plan's share package, contract type and web pieces are sound, but nothing wires the feature into the real API: apps/api/internal/http/routes.go and routes_test.go are owned by no task. Executed as written, the handler tests pass against share.Register directly while the running server returns 404 for both share endpoints, and acceptance criterion 4 (405 through the real router) has no task and no test. Give both files to the api task with route-level done criteria. Beyond that, fix the JSON wire shape of ShareLink in writing, decide what the owner sees after clicking Share (and when the clipboard fails), and say whether repeat POSTs mint new links. The baseline could not be re-run here; this is from reading the code only. | BLOCKS (blocker/high): No task owns routes.go, so nobody adds share.Register to http.Register, the only place features are wired ("Add new features here"). The api task's handler tests can pass by handing share.Register straight to testutil.NewServer, so `make test` goes green while the real server answers 404 on both POST /schedules/:id/share and GET /share/:token. The Share button and the public page would then have nothing to call. | BLOCKS (blocker/high): Acceptance criterion 4 (POST /share/:token returns 405, "api test through the real router") appears in no task's done, and routes_test.go, the only place that tests http.Register, is owned by no task. The criterion is tested by nobody. | BLOCKS (major/medium): The wire shape of ShareLink is fixed only in the TypeScript type. The api task's done checks token and url but not scheduleId or the JSON key names, so a Go struct without camelCase tags (e.g. ScheduleID) would pass the api tests and break the web side. | BLOCKS (major/medium): "Copies the returned url" is the only outcome of clicking Share. The plan says nothing about what the owner sees on success, or what happens when navigator.clipboard is unavailable or rejects (insecure context, denied permission). In that case the owner clicks Share and gets no link, with no error, which misses "I click Share, get a link".

trials.label: proceed

Every acceptance criterion maps to a task with a matching done item, and the code already provides what the plan leans on: auth.Require, store.KV, config.WebOrigin, schedules.PublicView, the router's 405 for unrouted methods, apiPost, and the ScheduleView contract type. The raise_bar items tighten the tests around the round trip, signed-in viewers, the response field names, storage failures and clipboard feedback. Nothing blocks.
